description:
Optional tier for apps that outgrow Cloudflare Containers (20 instances, 4 vCPU / 12 GiB, no guaranteed always-on). The dply Worker stays the front door (domains, TLS, firewall, previews); it forwards to a DigitalOcean Kubernetes cluster instead of a Cloudflare container.

Cloudflare parity already shipped 2026-09-24: in-flight autoscaling (fill instances in order, spill when full), min instances (never sleep), /_dply/warm after deploy, Inertia SSR auto-detected. Build this tier only when a paying customer actually hits a Cloudflare limit.

Shape: Knative Serving (scale to zero, holds requests while a sleeping app starts, concurrency autoscaling with containerConcurrency = requestsPerInstance), gVisor RuntimeClass for untrusted code, one namespace per org with NetworkPolicy + ResourceQuota. Reuse Providers/DigitalOcean client. Same image generator (EdgeContainerDockerfile) and same /_dply/queue and /_dply/schedule contract.

Effort: 1–2 weeks to a cluster that serves one app; 2–3 weeks to wire it into dply with metering; 1–2 months for wakes under a second; after that, ongoing ops work (upgrades, capacity, on-call).
title: Dedicated compute tier: containers on our own Kubernetes (DOKS + Knative)
